name: What is the difference between smooth and textured drywall finishes?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between smooth and textured drywall finishes?

acceptedAnswer.text: A smooth drywall finish involves multiple layers of joint compound sanded to a perfectly flat, uniform surface, ready for paint. Textured finishes, on the other hand, incorporate patterns or designs created with joint compound, ranging from subtle orange peel to more pronounced knockdown or popcorn textures. The practical tradeoff is that a smooth finish typically offers a modern, clean aesthetic but highlights imperfections more readily and requires more meticulous work, often leading to higher labor costs. Textured finishes can help conceal minor surface flaws and offer a different aesthetic, but can be harder to repair seamlessly if damaged.
acceptedAnswer.description: Smooth drywall finishes are flat and uniform, while textured finishes have patterns; smooth requires more precise work and can cost more.
